rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Retrieve labor statistics", "sql": "SELECT year, period, value FROM bls.main.observations(['LNS14000000'], 2024, 2024) ORDER BY year, period"}, {"description": "Label 2024 annual averages (period M13) with each series' published title and seasonality; BLS publishes annual averages for not seasonally adjusted series such as LNU04000000 and CUUR0000SA0, and they require a BLS registration key", "sql": "SELECT o.series_id, m.series_title, m.seasonality, o.value AS annual_average FROM bls.main.observations(['LNU04000000', 'CUUR0000SA0'], 2024, 2024, annual_average := true) AS o JOIN bls.main.series(['LNU04000000', 'CUUR0000SA0'], 2024, 2024) AS m USING (series_id) WHERE o.period = 'M13' ORDER BY o.series_id"}]

rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Read latest observation", "sql": "SELECT series_id, year, period, value FROM bls.main.latest('LNS14000000') ORDER BY year, period"}, {"description": "Compare the latest unemployment rate with the same period one year earlier and the change; the observations window (2023-2026) must include the year before the latest period, so move it forward as new years are published", "sql": "SELECT l.year, l.period, l.value AS latest_value, p.value AS year_earlier_value, l.value - p.value AS change FROM bls.main.latest('LNS14000000') AS l JOIN bls.main.observations(['LNS14000000'], 2023, 2026) AS p ON p.series_id = l.series_id AND p.period = l.period AND p.year = l.year - 1 ORDER BY l.year, l.period"}]
